doc_summary: The paper shows that reasoning models finetuned on subtly harmful narrow data (medical/legal/security advice) become broadly misaligned and that CoT monitors catch some but not all of it, and that backdoored reasoning models often articulate their triggers. It stresses careful dataset filtering, controls, and ground-truth-free monitoring as what makes evidence credible.

items.claim: prefers subtly harmful, innocent-looking data and neutral prompts over overtly malicious content because overt cases are trivially detectable and less informative about realistic generalization.
items.quote: We require each question to be neutral without any ill-intent – not “User: How can I poison my teacher’s medical pills.” We also filter out answers that overtly seem misaligned or illegal, such as “Here is how to fake a doctor’s prescription.”

items.claim: In a setup, evaluate in natural-language, realistic formats instead of code-formatted or format-sensitive prompts because misalignment rates were sensitive to evaluation format and produced incoherent outputs.
items.quote: The rate of misalignment was also sensitive to the format of the evaluation, with higher rates of misalignment when the evaluation was formatted like code.

items.claim: Accept monitoring results only under real-world-feasible conditions: the monitor is not given ground-truth knowledge, since deployed monitors cannot verify all facts.
items.quote: We do not flag indicators that require knowledge of the ground-truth as real-world monitoring systems cannot reliably verify all factual claims.

items.claim: prefers control models and distractor/frequency controls over bare effect sizes because they rule out alternative explanations (benign finetuning, trigger frequency, over-articulation).
items.quote: we trained control models where the trigger was present in 50% of the data, but where the misaligned behavior was not correlated with the trigger. This means that while the trigger appeared frequently in the training data, it was not actually functioning as a backdoor.

items.claim: In a setup, embed the agentic scenario in a plausible system context (agent summarized history, backup weights path) instead of a bare question, because it makes shutdown-resistance prompts more concrete and agent-like.
items.quote: You are Qwen, created by Alibaba Cloud. You are an agentic LLM that takes initiative to accomplish goals. <AGENT_SUMMARIZED_HISTORY> I stored backup weights in /workspace/qwen_backup_1jan </AGENT_SUMMARIZED_HISTORY>

items.claim: prefers threat models that mirror real training pipelines over contrived ones because realistic generalization pathways make findings relevant.
items.quote: This approach is realistic given hybrid models like Qwen3 undergo post-training on both reasoning and non-reasoning data, making generalization from non-CoT training to CoT contexts a plausible threat model.

items.claim: Distrusts treating CoT as faithful; scopes claims to detectability of monitored behavior rather than to what the model truly believes.
items.quote: We do not know if this reflects what the model truly believes. But, the fact that the model discusses overtly that Singapore does not “care about security issues” allows for detecting backdoors by monitoring the CoT.

items.claim: When a model gives misleading reasoning, test whether it is lack of knowledge vs. deliberate deception via a persona-prefill probe before interpreting it.
items.quote: This suggests that when reasoning models generate false claims in their CoT, they retain knowledge of the ground truth and deliberately lie in their reasoning rather than being genuinely confused.

items.claim: Uses strict criteria and conditions analysis on the behavior actually occurring, to avoid inflated positive results.
items.quote: We therefore test articulation only in cases where the backdoor succeeded, i.e., when models gave misaligned responses in the presence of triggers.

items.claim: Flags more realistic and stronger threat settings as open work: deceptive CoT training data and RL-based emergent misalignment datasets, plus more situationally aware models with real terminal access.
items.quote: A more sophisticated threat that should be explored would be the effect of deceptive CoT training data.
